llm_narrative: Across the 500 evaluation tasks the granite4.1_8b_output model achieved a mean claim‑coverage of only 0.0584 (median 0) despite an apparently high pass‑rate at the 0.75 threshold (80 %). The dominant failure mode was early termination, accounting for 202 of the 496 diagnosed failures (≈41 %), followed by task misunderstanding (97 cases, ≈20 %) and wrong‑tool selection (82 cases, ≈17 %). Only 166 failures (33.5 % of the total) involved a tool‑call error, whereas 330 failures (66.5 %) were purely cognitive – the model either stopped after gathering data or misinterpreted the prompt, leaving the reasoning chain unfinished. A concrete remediation is to augment the prompting/fine‑tuning pipeline with an explicit “final synthesis” checkpoint that forces the assistant to verify that all required claims have been addressed before ending the turn. What sets granite4.1_8b_output apart from other models is its relatively good ability to issue correct tool calls (the majority of tool‑related attempts succeeded) but a systematic inability to transition from data collection to answer generation, resulting in 226 empty responses (45 % of runs).
